fixes.explanation: That's the job, friend. The LORD tells Moses to "Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites." (Numbers 27:12) The land is already given, and Moses gets the view. I bet that climb had him huffing, but what a front-row seat.

Nobody is mentioned waiting up there with Moses, friend. The LORD says, "Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites." (Numbers 27:12) The elders aren't in this verse. Moses isn't headed to a meeting, and nobody is saving him a seat. The LORD gives him one job, which is to look.

Aaron it is. God says Moses will be gathered to his people "…as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) The next verse says why, and it names both brothers, because both of them rebelled against God's command at the waters. So the brothers' stories line up right to the end.

That's it, friend. Moses has just heard he'll be gathered to his people, and he doesn't start with himself. He asks the LORD to "…appoint a man over the congregation…" (Numbers 27:16) I think that's a man thinking about the people he's leaving behind. Even with that news, his mind is on them.

Yes, sheep. Moses asks for a leader so that "…the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) Sheep with no shepherd are like a batch of cookies with nobody watching the timer. Nobody is looking out for them, and that's how things end up burnt. Jesus uses this same picture when He sees the crowds and has compassion on them. (Matthew 9:36)

Travelers is a fair guess, but Moses doesn't reach for a map. He says, "…so that the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) Sheep can't read a map, friend. A shepherd goes out and comes in before them, and the verse before this one asks for exactly that kind of leader.

Spirit is right. God calls Joshua "…a man with the Spirit in him…" (Numbers 27:18) Look at what God points to. He doesn't read out a résumé. He names who is in the man. That's the description God gives right here when He tells Moses who to take.

That's the reason, friend. God says, "Confer on him some of your authority, so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him." (Numbers 27:20) Notice it says some of Moses' authority, and the point is that the people will follow him. A new leader with nothing behind him gets a lot of shrugs, and this one gets backing in front of everybody.

True. The text says, "Moses did as the LORD had commanded him." (Numbers 27:22) Then it shows him doing it. He took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation. The verse doesn't mention any delay. I've taken longer to follow a cookie recipe, and that one had pictures.
